To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) small atomic actions, like stealing a Contact or sending an SMS, have large hardware footprints and (b) obfuscation techniques make malware more detectable by HMDs.

(i) EMMA is the first platform that enables rigorous and comprehensive evaluation of HMDs; (ii) EMMA drives the state-of-the-art in HMD research, by identifying a set of 20 small atomic actions that are surprisingly detectable; and (iii) EMMA shows that obfuscation techniques, which are used to evade static analysis, can be leveraged to make malware detectable using HMs.

(1) EMMA is a new platform to evaluate HMDs for Android, (2) EMMA’s systematic approach to evaluate HMD algorithms is more effective than prior work, and (3) EMMA shows that the hardware footprint of atomic malware actions is surprisingly large.
